rationale: bugs_open/396's standing residual: park_work_items() (migration 621, WII-034) requires p_parked_by and p_parked_reason, but NOTHING stops a raw `UPDATE site_work_items SET status='deferred'`. A row at status='deferred' WITH a named handler_agent is selected by nothing — claim_work_item takes triaged/approved, the promoter takes detected — and still holds its idx_swi_dedup slot, so the detector cannot re-file it and any other session dispatching that page hits 23505, a failure that reads as 'already queued' and means 'queued and abandoned'. One such row blocked bugs_open/328 for 22 days and completed 2 minutes after being re-armed. The bug's §6 ranks this candidate first precisely because it makes the bad state unrepresentable rather than detectable. Migration 690 adds a BEFORE INSERT OR UPDATE trigger that refuses the transition into 'deferred' with a named handler unless the same write carries parked_by AND parked_reason. SCOPE IS SET BY A CENSUS, NOT BY THE BUG FILE: it fires ONLY on the named-handler shape, because 'deferred' + EMPTY handler_agent is a different and legitimate mechanism (the bugs_closed/077 shelf) used by five live producers — measured 2026-09-02, shelf = 2,656 rows carrying zero provenance and correctly so, versus 257 rows of the 396 shape of which 170 are unattributable. A guard requiring provenance on every 'deferred' write would have refused all 2,656 and broken those producers. Two design points came from reading the source rather than the bug file: provenance is accepted in EITHER spec OR result, because migration 389 writes spec and park_work_items() writes result (reading only spec is the exact misstep recorded in 396's own handoff §8.1, where 62 fully-stamped rows were reported as carrying no trace at all); and the guard fires only on the TRANSITION into deferred, so the 170 legacy unstamped rows stay writable and work_item_retraction.go can still drain them. I am submitting this having tested it but WITHOUT having applied it — the production apply is gated in my session — so the reviewers are reading a change that is committed and inert, and schema_migrations has no 690 row.

plan.summary: bugs_open/396: migration 690 adds a BEFORE INSERT OR UPDATE trigger on site_work_items that refuses a transition into status='deferred' with a NAMED handler_agent unless the same write carries parked_by AND parked_reason (in spec or result). Closes the bug's standing residual — nothing previously stopped a raw UPDATE. Scope set by a live census: the deferred + EMPTY handler 'shelf' class (2,656 rows, five producers, correctly provenance-free) is explicitly exempt, as are already-deferred rows so the retraction drain still works. Ships with a one-statement withdrawal lever and a behavioural VERIFY; mutation-proved in both directions.

edits.rationale: Creates refuse_untraceable_park() and attaches trg_site_work_items_park_provenance BEFORE INSERT OR UPDATE on site_work_items. Three exits before any refusal keep the blast radius at the measured shape: not 'deferred' -> pass; empty handler_agent -> pass (the 2,656-row shelf class); already 'deferred' on UPDATE -> pass (so the retraction drain and the 170 legacy rows are unaffected). Only then is provenance required, read from spec OR result. The file proves itself before COMMIT: the post-check INDUCES the refusal on a synthetic row and aborts the migration if the guard does not fire, because a verify block made of SELECTs cannot stop a COMMIT (ON_ERROR_STOP ignores a non-empty result set). Preconditions refuse to install if the trigger already exists or if the shelf-class census returns zero, i.e. if the scope reasoning was never true here.

The withdrawal lever, and it is deliberately one statement so it can be used under pressure without reading the file: DROP TRIGGER takes effect immediately, needs no image roll, and leaves the function in place so re-arming is a single CREATE TRIGGER. The full file also drops the function. Its header states plainly what is being turned back on rather than describing the mechanics, so the decision to withdraw is an informed one.

Re-provable after apply, and behavioural rather than structural. It INDUCES the refusal on synthetic rows and ends in ROLLBACK. Six assertions, and the two-sidedness is the point: 1 and 6 prove it refuses (on UPDATE and on INSERT), 2 proves half a provenance is not provenance, 3/4/5 prove it does NOT refuse the sanctioned verb, the shelf class, or an already-deferred row. A one-sided 'did it refuse?' test would pass a guard that refused everything while breaking 2,656 live rows. A `SELECT ... FROM pg_trigger` check is kept only as a precondition, because that a trigger is ATTACHED says nothing about what it does — the same lane was caught by exactly that a week earlier, when a nominated guard turned out to be a substring test returning HONOURS on four spellings including two that switched the rule off.

grounded_in: bugs_open/396 §6 candidate 1: 'Make an untraceable park impossible. A park writes spec.parked_by + parked_reason or it does not happen — enforced where the write happens, not by convention. Migration 389 is already the model.'
bugs_open/396 residual, restated in HANDOFF_2026-08-26b §6: 'Nothing stops a raw UPDATE … SET status=deferred. Short of a database trigger, nothing can.'

write_audit_findings_action.go:95 — the codebase already names the discriminator: the record-mode shape is 'deferred' + empty handler_agent, and the comment warns against 'the other shape — deferred WITH a named handler, no ...'.

write_build_items_routing_test.go — asserts the gap row carries an EMPTY handler: 'capability_gap carried handler_agent %q, want empty — a deferred row naming an agent that does not exist is bugs_closed/078's shape'.
Census 2026-09-02 on live clients_db: deferred + empty handler = 2,656 rows, 0 with provenance; deferred + named handler = 257 rows, 87 with provenance (all parked_by='migration_389'), 170 without.

621_park_work_items_verb.sql:147-154 — the verb writes provenance into `result`, not `spec`: SET status='deferred', result = COALESCE(w.result,'{}') || jsonb_build_object('parked_by', ..., 'parked_reason', ..., 'parked_from_status', w.status, 'parked_by_verb','park_work_items').
389_park_contrast_failures...sql:80-83 — writes the same three keys into `spec`, so a guard reading only one location would refuse one of the two sanctioned writers.

CHECK constraint swi_no_handlerless_promotable = NOT (handler_agent='' AND status IN ('triaged','approved','claimed')) — found by the dry run rejecting the first draft of the test, which staged a shelf row at 'triaged'.

Mutation evidence 2026-09-02, both dry runs ending in ROLLBACK: guard made inert -> assertion 1 fails 'an untraceable park was ACCEPTED', exit 3; shelf exemption removed -> assertion 4 fails 'the SHELF class (deferred + empty handler) was REFUSED', exit 3. The clean run passes all 6 with exit 0.
